q: How far is the Varanasi cricket stadium from Cantt station?
a: Roughly 15–18 km by road. It usually takes 40–60 minutes on a normal day; allow much longer on match days. We'll replace these estimates with times we've measured ourselves.

q: How far is the stadium from Varanasi airport?
a: About 20–25 km by road from Lal Bahadur Shastri airport at Babatpur. Allow at least an hour, more on match days.

q: Which railway station is closest to the stadium?
a: Banaras station (Manduadih) looks slightly closer to Ganjari than Varanasi Junction (Cantt) on the map. Cantt has far more trains and cabs, though, so most visitors will still start there. We'll confirm the better option once we've driven both routes.

q: How long does it take to reach the stadium from the ghats?
a: Expect about an hour on a normal day, longer on match days. Much of that time goes in getting out of the old-city lanes, not on the highway.

q: Can I take an auto to the stadium?
a: Yes, autos and cabs both go to Ganjari. Agree the fare before you get in, and on match days expect fares to go up.

q: Will there be shuttle buses on match days?
a: Nothing official has been announced yet. If the authorities run shuttles, we'll add the pick-up points here.

q: Is it safe to come back late at night after a match?
a: The highway is busy and lit near the city, but cabs can be hard to find after a big match. Book your return ride in advance or agree a wait with your driver.
